Exercise A

Listening: Book Character Day

You will hear each recording twice, just like in the real MSA exam. Listen carefully, then answer the questions below — you won't be able to play a recording more than twice.

Part 1 — Library Announcement
Part 1 — Comprehension Questions

1 When is Book Character Day?

2 Who judges the costume competition?

3 What does the winner receive?

4 What can students do instead of dressing up?

5 When must written entries be handed in?

Part 2 — Dialogue: Two Friends
Part 2 — Comprehension Questions

6 Who is Marcus dressing as?

Exercise B

Reading: Character Types & Competition Rules

Read the texts below, then answer the questions — just like Reading Parts 1 and 2 in the real MSA exam.

Part 1 — Match the Student to the Character Type

The Leader: Always puts the team first and makes brave decisions under pressure.

The Inventor: Solves problems with clever gadgets and never stops asking "what if?"

The Outsider: Doesn't fit in at first, but turns out to have a hidden talent that saves the day.

The Best Friend: Always there to support the hero, even when things get difficult.

1 Leo admires people who are brave and take charge in difficult situations. His favourite type is .

2 Ava loves building and inventing things in her free time. Her favourite type is .

3 Noah felt like he didn't fit in at his old school but found his place. His favourite type is .

4 Sofia values loyalty above everything else in a friendship. Her favourite type is .

Part 2 — Competition Notice: True or False?

🎭 Costumes must be based on a character from a book, film, or comic.

🕐 The costume competition takes place during lunchtime on Wednesday.

📌 Writing entries will be displayed on the library wall, not read aloud.

💰 Entry to both competitions is completely free.

5 Costumes can only be based on characters from books.

6 The costume competition happens during lunchtime.

7 Writing entries are read aloud in assembly.

8 There is a cost to enter the competitions.

Exercise C

Writing: Blog Post

Choose ONE of the two prompts below and write 80–100 words, just like Writing Part 3 in the real MSA exam. This section is graded by your teacher, not automatically.

Choose ONE prompt

Prompt 1: Describe your favourite fictional character and explain why you admire them.

Prompt 2: Imagine you could be a fictional character for a day. Who would you choose, and what would you do?
